story_type: launch pad emergency escape basket ride, onboard camera
hook: If the moon rocket catches fire, this basket is the way down.
narration: If a moon rocket catches fire on the pad, this basket is the way down.
It hangs off the launch tower at Pad 39B, three hundred seventy five feet up.
Four of them wait up there, each about the size of a small SUV.
Each one rides a cable one thousand three hundred thirty five feet long.
Magnets brake the basket as it rolls, the same trick roller coasters use to slow down.
outcome: The basket rolled into the landing zone at the bottom of the pad, at the end of its quarter mile cable.
title: Moon rocket escape basket ride
description:
A camera rides one of the Artemis emergency escape baskets at Launch Pad 39B, NASA Kennedy Space Center, Florida (July 2024). In a pad emergency, these baskets carry astronauts and pad crews down 1,335-foot cables to the edge of the pad.

Footage: NASA Kennedy Space Center video, via the NASA Image and Video Library: https://images.nasa.gov/details/KSC-20240712-VP-MWC01-001-ARTEMIS-360-BASKET-REFRAME-M7145

extra_sources.excerpt: Located on the 274-foot-level, teams are approximately 375 feet above the ground. From there, they will head down the 1,335-foot-long cables inside the emergency egress baskets to the launch pad perimeter. Each basket, which is similar in size to a small SUV, is designed to carry up to five people or a maximum weight of 1,500 pounds. We have four baskets that sit on the side of the mobile launcher tower
We have a new magnetic braking system for the Artemis emergency egress system, which involves using magnetics to help slow down a vehicle
